entry.title: Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity
entry.summary: We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior Hölder estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.

entry.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
entry.summary: We give a detailed implementation of the mass-splitting construction of Nazarov, Volberg and Yuditskii for reflectionless measures with singular continuous components. The finite approximants are allowed to have isolated atoms. An exact local operation replaces each active atom by a short permanent interval and two child atoms, thereby eliminating the dependence of a future splitting scale on an already prescribed band width. Summable estimates for completed generations and fixed cylinders retain positive mass on a null Cantor set and exclude atoms in the limit. Uniform analytic estimates near the permanent intervals establish reflectionlessness and exclude endpoint singularities. A separate Green function estimate for thin pairs of intervals gives the Widom condition and regularity of the limiting compact set. The resulting probability measure has both a nonzero absolutely continuous component and a nonzero singular continuous component.

entry.title: Unbounded Widom factors for orthogonal and residual polynomials
entry.summary: We study Widom factors for (a) monic orthogonal polynomials in $L^2$ with respect to the equilibrium measure of a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ and (b) residual polynomials normalized at an exterior point. Using weakly equilibrium Cantor sets $K(γ)$, we prove: (1) Given any sequence $(c_n)$ with subexponential growth, there exists a non-polar Cantor set $K(γ)$, depending on $(c_n)$, such that the $L^2$ Widom factors of the associated orthogonal polynomials (with respect to the equilibrium measure of $K(γ)$) exceed $c_n$ for every $n$. (2) For the same $K(γ)$ built from $(c_n)$ and each exterior point $x_0\in\mathbb{R}\setminus K(γ)$, the residual Widom factors satisfy power-type lower bounds with a Harnack-distance exponent $τ_{x_0}\in(0,1)$: they are bounded below by $c_n^{τ_{x_0}}$ for all degrees when $x_0$ lies in an unbounded gap, and along a subsequence of degrees when $x_0$ lies in a bounded gap. Consequently, if, in addition, $(c_n)$ is monotone increasing and unbounded, then the sequence of residual Widom factors is unbounded for every $x_0\in\mathbb{R}\setminus K(γ)$. The proofs combine inverse-image constructions, capacity comparisons for period-$n$ sets, harmonic-measure representations for differences of Green functions, and alternation principles on nested approximants.

entry.title: Vladimirov-Pearson Operators on $ζ$-regular Ultrametric Cantor Sets
entry.summary: A new operator for certain types of ultrametric Cantor sets is constructed using the measure coming from the spectral triple associated with the Cantor set, as well as its zeta function. Under certain mild conditions on that measure, it is shown that it is an integral operator similar to the Vladimirov-Taibleson operator on the p-adic integers. Its spectral properties are studied, and the Markov property and kernel representation of the heat kernel generated by this so-called \emph{Vladimirov-Pearson} operator is shown, viewed as acting on a certain Sobolev space. A large class of these operators have a heat kernel and a Green function explicitly given by the ultrametric wavelets on the Cantor set, which are eigenfunctions of the operator.

entry.title: Cantor sets with absolutely continuous harmonic measure
entry.summary: We construct Ahlfors regular Cantor sets $K$ of small dimension in the plane, such that the Hausdorff measure on $K$ is equivalent to the harmonic measure associated to its complement. In particular the Green function in $R^2 \backslash K$ satisfies $G^p (x) \simeq \mathrm{dist} (x, K)^δ$ whenever $\mathrm{dist} (x, K) \le 1$ and $p$ is far from $K$.
